summary: All seven source fields have been assessed. No end-to-end mapping is confirmed yet. Start with intended Shopify behavior, quantity meaning and location scope.

target_candidates.name: Inventory synchronization
target_candidates.when: If the feed owns absolute stock totals and is intended to update inventory.

target_candidates.name: Availability display
target_candidates.when: If this interface supplies customer-facing availability. Storefront fields can be read; custom date/message storage needs a separate design.

observations.text: The embedded WSDL schema defines seven optional fields. Dates are dateTime, quantity is int, InStock is boolean, and the remaining fields are strings.
Nine records: eight in stock and one out of stock. The zero-stock record has 2049-12-31 and Not Available. This co-occurrence does not establish a business rule.
The pasted excerpt is incomplete XML. A separate normalized copy adds only the two missing closing tags.

The sample repeats WebAvailabilityData directly. The WSDL uses GetWebItemAvailabilityResponse → GetWebItemAvailabilityResult → WebAvailabilityData → WebAvailabilityItem. Origin or transformation is unknown.

Shopify mutation examples/prose include legacy compareQuantity wording. The 2026-07 input reference specifies changeFromQuantity. This POC follows that input reference; no live schema validation has run.

mappings.reason: Meaning, timezone and customer display requirements are unknown.
mappings.proposed_rule: Preserve raw value. Consider a custom field only after agreeing its meaning; do not treat 2049-12-31 as a confirmed delivery date.

mappings.reason: An empty element and Not Available are observed; their rules are unknown.
mappings.proposed_rule: Preserve the difference between empty, absent and populated values. Custom display data is a candidate only.

mappings.reason: The source quantity meaning, authority and location scope have not been established.
mappings.proposed_rule: If confirmed as an authoritative absolute sellable total for a mapped location, propose name=available and use the integer value. Zero remains zero; missing is not zero.

mappings.target: No direct writable field in the selected candidate
mappings.reason: The inventory mutation has no InStock input. Storefront availableForSale is a read result, not a write mapping.
mappings.proposed_rule: Retain for rule analysis; do not map to a read-only availability field or silently discard.

mappings.reason: Requires a confirmed identity rule and a unique match in the actual Shopify store.
mappings.proposed_rule: Keep as text. Resolve the Shopify inventory item ID; reject missing or ambiguous matches. Do not select the first match blindly.

mappings.reason: Only N appears in this sample; its meaning and other values are unknown.
mappings.proposed_rule: No product-type translation, filter or exclusion until the code list and rules are confirmed.

mappings.reason: It equals SKU in this sample; that does not establish a general identity rule.
mappings.proposed_rule: Keep as text. Do not substitute this value for a Shopify product, variant or inventory ID.

questions.question: What should Shopify do with this feed?
questions.hint: Update sellable stock, display delivery/availability information, or both?
questions.why: Determines whether an inventory write is the right target.

questions.question: Where is this XML produced?
questions.hint: ERP, middleware, Sitecore, or an export? Please also provide a complete response if available.
questions.why: The sample wrapper differs from the WSDL and is missing two closing tags.

questions.question: What does AvailableQuantity represent?
questions.hint: Is this an absolute total or a change? Sellable stock or physical stock? Which system owns it?
questions.why: An absolute inventory set is suitable only if the source owns the inventory total.

questions.question: Which location does the quantity belong to?
questions.hint: One warehouse/location, a combined total, or separate values elsewhere?
questions.why: Shopify inventory writes need a location ID; none is supplied.

questions.question: How do these identifiers match Shopify?
questions.hint: Does SKU match the Shopify SKU? Can duplicates exist? What does WebProductId identify?
questions.why: Resolve actual inventory IDs; do not turn an ERP identifier into a Shopify ID.

questions.question: What do the availability dates mean?
questions.hint: Meaning of 2049-12-31, timezone, empty date range, and whether customers should see these values.
questions.why: A possible sentinel date must not become a real delivery promise.

questions.question: What controls InStock?
questions.hint: Is it derived from quantity, or does it include backorders, fulfilment or other rules?
questions.why: A source flag is not automatically equivalent to Shopify availability for sale.

questions.question: What does SKUType mean?
questions.hint: Please explain N, other possible values and any special processing.
questions.why: Product type rules could change how identity and inventory should be handled.

questions.question: How is the feed delivered?
questions.hint: Schedule or event? Full snapshot or partial feed? What should happen to missing, duplicate, late or failed records?
questions.why: Defines processing rules beyond individual field assignments.

target_requirements.note: available or on_hand; choose after confirming quantity meaning.
Resolve using confirmed identity rules and actual store data.
Location mapping is absent. Combined stock must not be copied into each warehouse.
Read the expected current quantity. An explicit null skips the concurrency check and needs an agreed policy.
Choose the documented reason matching the agreed business event.
Define one key per logical request and reuse it on retries.
Consider a source document or batch reference for traceability.

interface_gates.description: Choose stock synchronization, availability display, or both.
Confirm source contract and payload origin.
Confirm identity, quantity ownership, locations and product-type rules.
Define scheduling, retries, partial failures and stale-message handling.
Validate schema, permissions, inventory tracking and location activation in a Shopify test store.

evidence.title: Checkout WSDL with embedded schemas
evidence.note: GetWebItemAvailability has no request fields. WebAvailabilityItem defines all seven sample fields; each is optional.

evidence.title: User-provided availability excerpt
evidence.note: Nine records: eight positive quantities and one zero. SKU and WebProductId match in these nine examples only.

evidence.title: Inventory write
evidence.note: Sets absolute quantities. Requires write_inventory and inventory update permission. Use for an authoritative stock source. Version 2026-07 requires an idempotency key.

evidence.title: Inventory set input
evidence.note: name, reason and quantities are required. name accepts available or on_hand. referenceDocumentUri is optional.

evidence.title: Per-item quantity input
evidence.note: inventoryItemId, locationId and quantity are non-null. changeFromQuantity must be explicitly supplied, even though its type is nullable. Prefer a current quantity value for concurrency checking.

evidence.title: Inventory item lookup
evidence.note: inventoryItems supports filtering by SKU. Search results must be checked for exact matching and ambiguity.

evidence.title: Inventory locations
evidence.note: locations provides location records. Business rules must identify the correct destination.

evidence.title: Customer-facing availability
evidence.note: ProductVariant exposes availableForSale and quantityAvailable as read fields. These are not writable destinations for this source feed.

evidence.title: Custom field alternative
evidence.note: metafieldsSet can store custom data. Owner, namespace, key, type and business meaning would need a separate design.

evidence.title: Inventory activation
evidence.note: inventoryActivate establishes an inventory item at a location. Existing activation must be checked before quantity updates.

validation_scenarios.expected: Keep zero as an explicit value. Do not infer confirmed stock semantics from the sample.
Flag a missing value; never silently set stock to zero.
Require resolution; do not invent an ID or use an arbitrary search result.
Hold the proposed write until allocation is defined.
Keep original values and request the rule; do not publish an inferred delivery promise.

validation_scenarios.scenario: Retry, concurrency conflict or older source message
validation_scenarios.expected: Apply the agreed idempotency and ordering rules. Those rules remain unresolved.

changes: Initial analysis from two supplied WSDLs, nine sample records and official Shopify documentation.
limitations: AI-assisted draft; business decisions are unconfirmed.
Public documentation research only. No Shopify MCP or live store connection was used.
The report collects answers but does not run an AI model. Re-analysis is a separate assistant step.
